terms.definition: A boundary within which a domain model and its terminology have one consistent meaning.
A responsibility and interface boundary that limits coupling between deployable or modular parts.
The explicit authority responsible for creating, changing, retaining, and deleting a data set.
A composition organized into layers with controlled dependency direction and responsibility separation.
A single deployable with enforceable internal modules and explicit interfaces.
A sequence of processing stages where each stage transforms data for the next stage.
A minimal core extended by replaceable plugins or adapters.
A system composed of coarse-grained services communicating through explicit contracts.
A system where producers publish events and consumers react asynchronously to facts about state changes.
A system that distributes processing and state across nodes to reduce centralized bottlenecks.
A system where a coordinator explicitly controls a multi-step workflow across participants.
Independently deployable services organized around bounded business capabilities.
A hierarchical notation for communicating context, containers, components, and code-level structure.
A modeling approach that aligns software boundaries and language with domain concepts and business capabilities.
A separation of command/write models from query/read models when their responsibilities or scaling needs differ.
A persistence approach that records state changes as an append-only event history from which state is reconstructed.
A distributed-system trade-off between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance during network partitions.
A consistency model in which replicas converge when updates stop and communication succeeds.
The property that repeating an operation produces the same intended effect as performing it once.
A mechanism that limits producers or queues when consumers cannot safely keep up.
A boundary where every request is authenticated, authorized, minimized, and evaluated without implicit network trust.
A deployment model where one system serves multiple customers while preserving tenant isolation and policy boundaries.
The ability to infer internal system behavior from structured logs, metrics, traces, and meaningful operational events.
A tested way to return a change or deployment to a known safe state without losing required data or evidence.
